meta_title: Sri Lanka Passport Photo Rules: Digital Studio Photos | Resize-It
meta_description: Sri Lankan passport photos must be digital, taken by an authorised studio and sent online. Printed photos are not accepted. Rules on glasses, scarves and photo age.
subtitle: How Sri Lanka's digital passport photo system works, and how to check your look before the studio visit.

tool_workspace.description: Upload a photo to crop it to the official size. Everything is processed in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
tool_workspace.spec_background: Background: Set by the authorised studio

rows.label: Photo type
rows.value: Digital only. Printed photographs are not accepted for passport applications.

rows.label: Who takes it
rows.value: An authorised photo studio, or the Department head office or a regional office

rows.label: How it is sent
rows.value: The studio sends your photo online to the Department and gives you a Studio Acknowledgement Note

rows.label: Glasses
rows.value: Eyes must be clearly visible without spectacles

rows.label: Caps and scarves
rows.value: Allowed, but your forehead and ears must be clearly visible with no scarf shadows on your face

rows.label: Applying abroad
rows.value: Applications through Sri Lankan missions overseas can be made without the digital photograph and fingerprints

notes: You cannot submit a photo you made yourself for a Sri Lankan passport. The authorised studio captures and sends it.
Bring the Studio Acknowledgement Note with your application and supporting documents.
Fingerprints are collected in person at the head office or regional offices for applicants aged 16–60.
You can still use this tool to preview framing, or to make photos for other documents that accept prints.

how_to.title: How to make a Sri Lankan passport photo
how_to.step1_text: Read the Sri Lankan requirements below so you know what the studio will capture.
how_to.step2_text: Upload a test photo here to check framing, glasses and background before you go. Nothing leaves your browser.
how_to.step3_text: The official photo has to be taken and sent by an authorised studio or office.
how_to.step4_text: Bring the studio acknowledgement with your application.

items.q: Can I use a printed photo for a Sri Lankan passport?
items.a: No. Since August 2015 the Department only accepts digital photos sent by an authorised studio or captured at its offices.

items.q: Can I wear glasses in a Sri Lankan passport photo?
items.a: No. The studio instructions say your eyes must be clearly visible without spectacles.

items.q: Can I wear a scarf or cap?
items.a: Yes, as long as your forehead and ears are clearly visible and the scarf casts no shadow on your face.

items.q: How recent must the photo be?
items.a: It must have been taken within 6 months.
